title: Research map
summary: Known results, model cases and open directions in the non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor project. Follow a branch to its mathematical statements, definitions and source records.
readingNote: Branches group related work. Indentation denotes topic membership; it does not assert mathematical implication. Each linked result retains its stated hypotheses and source status.
scopeNote: The theory uses the fixed original field and absolute value, ordinary Berkovich neighborhoods, and the original CLD tests with actual refinements. Global energy results use strict Laurent boxes with extending backgrounds unless the linked statement says otherwise.

branches.title: Regularization and semipositive metrics
branches.summary: Approximation on a fixed neighborhood supplies the bounded and continuous potentials used by the product theory.

nodes.title: Approximation over the original field
nodes.summary: Locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic functions have decreasing semipositive rational piecewise-linear approximations on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. For continuous current-positive functions on smooth quasi-projective analytifications, smooth positive approximation is locally uniform and becomes decreasing after shrinking.

links.label: Bounded classical regularization
Continuous regularization

nodes.title: Projective semipositivity and envelopes
nodes.summary: Under the projective, ample and regular-model hypotheses, contact rigidity and curve approximation give the curve criterion and continuous orthogonal envelopes. The normal-model envelope extension has its own stated hypotheses.

links.label: Projective curve criterion
Normal-model envelopes

nodes.title: Toward finite-energy intersections
nodes.summary: The arithmetic extension asks for local finite-energy metric-change formulas and placewise summability compatible with the boundary completion. These are additional requirements beyond the established continuous local products.

links.label: Problem: Adelic finite-energy intersection

branches.title: Bounded products and differential calculus
branches.summary: The established bounded calculus constructs mixed currents and removes dependence on individual potential representatives.

nodes.title: Positive, symmetric bounded products
nodes.summary: For a fixed allowed positive closed background, bounded classical potentials give positive, separately closed, symmetric mixed currents. Local CLN estimates and weighted joint decreasing continuity retain the original analytic tests and actual refinements.

links.label: Bounded product theorem

nodes.title: Curvature classes, gluing and order completion
nodes.summary: Bounded classical potentials with equal curvatures give the same mixed products, so products of currents with such local potentials glue. The specified continuous-coefficient module, its piecewise-smooth differentials and its fixed-gauge order completion have intrinsic actions; variable coefficients need not give closed outputs.

links.label: Gluing local-potential currents
Coefficient module and order completion

nodes.title: Moving backgrounds and finite étale formulas
nodes.summary: For continuous current-positive potentials on smooth quasi-projective analytifications, locally uniform convergence permits weakly moving positive closed backgrounds. The bounded calculus also has the stated finite étale compatibility and degree formula under its morphism and normalization hypotheses.

links.label: Continuous potentials with moving closed positive backgrounds
Étale compatibility and the degree formula

nodes.title: Higher and variable-coefficient interfaces
nodes.summary: Construct the higher coupled quotient, variable piecewise-smooth coefficient actions, differential compatibility and full delta-test interfaces. Each extension requires its own object, test and mapping hypotheses.

links.label: Problem: Higher and variable-coefficient differential interfaces

branches.title: Capacity, quasicontinuity and comparison
branches.summary: Relative capacity controls bounded potentials and comparison. General Borel regularity remains a distinct question.

nodes.title: Relative comparison and the ambient case
nodes.summary: Bounded classical potentials are relatively quasicontinuous and decreasing approximations converge in capacity. A compact boundary gap gives comparison and relative quasi-everywhere domination. For the ambient background [1], the stated exhaustion hypotheses give polarity, Choquet capacity and Borel regularity.

links.label: Quasicontinuity and decreasing convergence
Comparison with a compact boundary gap
Ambient Choquet theorem

nodes.title: Parameter bands and finite-Hausdorff-measure sets
nodes.summary: Conormal Borel parameter bands give separately closed restrictions under the parameter-annihilation and disintegration hypotheses. In the specified torus boxes with q = 1 and S₀ = βⁿ⁻¹[X], outer capacity is inner regular on saturated Borel sets of finite (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure inside a compact moment subbox, including the stated one-sided background-order extension.

links.label: Closed parameter bands and conditional currents
Inner regularity on saturated sets of finite Hausdorff measure

nodes.title: Limits of universal capacity formulas
nodes.summary: Examples refute universal raw–outer equality, relative strong subadditivity and the extremal total-mass formula. These failures leave Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity open.

links.label: Failure of universal equality between raw and outer capacity
Failure of relative strong subadditivity
Failure of the relative extremal total-mass formula

nodes.title: General Borel regularity and tester recovery
nodes.summary: Determine Borel inner regularity for every allowed extending background on a strict Laurent box. Find additional hypotheses giving recovery by actual normalized testers and promotion of relative quasi-everywhere conclusions to specified pointwise representatives.

links.label: Question: Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity
Problem: Tester recovery and relative detection

branches.title: Unbounded potentials and finite energy
branches.summary: Truncation, capacity tails and a strong first-energy completion extend the bounded calculus under explicit mass and boundary conditions.

nodes.title: Non-polar products and capacity tails
nodes.summary: Non-polar products are separately closed when their coefficient masses are locally finite. On strict Laurent boxes with an extending background and compact negative sublevels, capacity tails characterize no loss of mass and every positive-power energy class. Mixed and level-current formulas retain their degree, integrability and tail conditions.

links.label: Truncation and capacity–energy estimates

nodes.title: A complete first-energy space
nodes.summary: On a strict Laurent box, with a fixed background extending past its closure and the stated boundary conditions, the completion has Borel representatives modulo relative outer-capacity zero, intrinsic mixed currents and Green–Hölder constant one. Strong convergence is equivalent to local truncated capacity convergence together with energy convergence. Relative rooftops, Perron envelopes and Borel obstacle problems are constructed in this completed order.

links.label: Complete first-energy space
Relative Perron envelopes

nodes.title: Sharp constants and critical tail conditions
nodes.summary: The rooftop energy constant cannot always be one. Energy boundedness and capacity convergence alone do not give critical continuity; the required no-loss and uniform-tail hypotheses must remain in the limiting statements.

links.label: The sharp obstruction to rooftop energy constant one
Critical continuity requires tail control

nodes.title: Relative singularity invariants
nodes.summary: For explicit potential and background classes, determine which non-polar masses, no-loss conditions and energies survive bounded changes of singularity. Begin with controlled model singularities and a stated proper-modification theorem.

links.label: Problem: Relative singularity invariants

branches.title: Source equations and Dirichlet problems
branches.summary: Variational projection gives an exact residual criterion for nonlinear sources. General data conditions and literal strong continuity remain open.

nodes.title: Projection and an exact source criterion
nodes.summary: On the stated Laurent domains, the energy-difference space is Banach and the nonlinear source image is norm closed. Strongly continuous dual data have a unique variational projection. For positive literal Radon data with bounded, strongly continuous integration, the scalar defect vanishes exactly when the source equation has a solution.

links.label: Banach space, projection and source criterion
The scalar defect and its equation

nodes.title: The remaining-degree-one Dirichlet equation
nodes.summary: When q = 1, a faithful regular strongly local coercive part form gives a unique renormalized zero-boundary solution for finite signed energy-diffuse data. The ambient dimension is unrestricted; the stated stability concerns fixed clippings and qualified curvature expressions in this part-energy space.

links.label: Remaining-degree-one Dirichlet theorem
Theorem 10.10 — Strong clipping and smooth-curvature stability

nodes.title: Explicit source families
nodes.summary: Prescribed parameter and radial families have source inverses under their energy and flux-tail conditions. Small Hölder constructions in specified smooth toric backgrounds retain the separate density, exterior-trace and interface compatibility hypotheses.

links.label: Parameter energy models and radial source inversion
Small nonradial interfaces and nonlinear source graphs

nodes.title: General literal data and compatible sources
nodes.summary: For one fixed background, ask whether bounded literal integration on the entire energy-difference space implies strong L¹ continuity, including the allowed infinite-mass case. Find conditions stated directly on the datum that also force the source defect to vanish; the fixed-background rooftop and finite-minorant criteria remain sufficient routes to be established in general.

links.label: Question: Literal energy-dual strong continuity
Problem: Checkable compatible source classes

nodes.title: Source-image and duality obstructions
nodes.summary: Even small positive smooth density perturbations can leave the nonlinear source image. Countable measure families and nonliteral duals also obstruct proposed shortcuts to capacity detection and literal integration; they do not settle the fixed-background literal-continuity question.

links.label: The nonlinear source image need not be open
Countable-measure and nonliteral-dual obstructions

branches.title: Descent of actual analytic relations
branches.summary: This branch asks whether relations between curvature expressions act trivially on every allowed background, beyond independence of individual potentials.

nodes.title: Degree one and approximable backgrounds
nodes.summary: Actual degree-one relations and the specified constant-coefficient ambient-cycle relations descend. Higher action also descends on W_loc, the ordinary-local weak closure of positive closed actual delta-backgrounds, with its full test class and required tail estimates.

links.label: Degree-one action and constant-coefficient cycle relations
Higher action on the local weak closure of geometric backgrounds

nodes.title: Proved sufficient criteria
nodes.summary: A zero carrier-CLN seminorm, or a full-exact approximation controlled by one fixed positive current before backgrounds, tests and refinements are chosen, forces action vanishing. Normal-current and harmonic-potential formulas provide supporting calculus under their own hypotheses. These are conditional criteria with proved implications.

links.label: Sufficient exactness criteria

nodes.title: Quadratic descent in joint residue rank at most two
nodes.summary: For quadratic actual analytic zero relations in finite continuous closed-cell piecewise-linear or piecewise-smooth presentations of joint residue rank at most two, the action vanishes for every allowed background, in arbitrary ambient dimension. The resulting quadratic action is canonical on germs of residue dimension at most two. Comparisons use the union tuple.

links.label: Joint residue rank: definition
Quadratic descent in rank at most two

nodes.title: General descent and stronger certificates
nodes.summary: Descent of all actual analytic relations remains open. Universal carrier certificates, fixed-control full-exact approximation and density of all allowed backgrounds are separate proposed routes. Sufficiency is established under their stated hypotheses; those hypotheses are not known in general.

links.label: Conjecture: Descent of actual analytic relations
Question: Carrier-CLN vanishing
Question: Local approximation of backgrounds

nodes.title: Primitive, gluing and lifting obstructions
nodes.summary: The recorded examples rule out proposed smooth double primitives, unrestricted Killing gluing, Jacobian-only piecewise-linear graph formulas and overly strong finite-unit lifting. Real finite-fan obstructions have not been realized as actual analytic zero relations, so they do not disprove general actual-relation descent.

links.label: Failure of continuous smooth-form double primitives
Real Killing-gluing and fixed-Q obstructions
Hessian-wall drift in PL graph pullback
Limits of finite unit lifting and Hensel boundary extension

branches.title: The critical normal-three model
branches.summary: In the supplied model, quadratic descent reduces to cancellation of a central residual determined by actual joint analytic data.

nodes.title: Curve stars and the whole central fiber
nodes.summary: The supplied normal-three model has marked-curve and unit-completion constructions, a paired Stokes identity and ordinary localization covering the whole protected central fiber. The required commensurability of radii and the order of completion and faithful separation remain part of the construction.

links.label: Actual curve stars, unit completion and joint Stokes
Ordinary localization around the whole central fiber

nodes.title: Punctured vanishing and a point residual
nodes.summary: For a fixed quadratic actual analytic zero in the supplied normal-three model, the action vanishes off the center for every allowed background. It also vanishes at the center below top degree; in top degree it equals a scalar multiple of the central Dirac measure.

links.label: Punctured action and the central residual

nodes.title: An explicit spherical residual formula
nodes.summary: For a quadratic actual analytic zero in the supplied normal-three model, protected transposition, critical trace-mass estimates and leading-jet bounds express the central residual as a spherical mass-minus-gradient pairing. The relation and background are jointly realized by the original analytic data; tangent uniqueness is not required.

links.label: Spherical formula for the residual

nodes.title: Cancellation for actual joint data
nodes.summary: Prove that the realized spherical pairing vanishes for every allowed degree-one background in the supplied normal-three model. The existing O(1) strip bound does not give the vanishing estimate needed for the general cancellation step.

links.label: Conjecture: Cancellation of the realized critical pairing

nodes.title: Critical mass growth alone is insufficient
nodes.summary: A real critical example shows that positivity, closedness and O(r²) mass growth can leave a point residual. It is not an actual-zero counterexample; cancellation must use the jointly realized analytic data.

links.label: Critical r² mass growth does not remove a point residual

branches.title: Domains, representatives and intersections
branches.summary: These extensions start from the established local and completed theories and pose additional geometric, representative and summability requirements.

nodes.title: Established starting points
nodes.summary: The Laurent-box theory supplies no-loss criteria, a strong Borel completion and global Green symmetry under its extending-background hypotheses. For the specified rational integrable adelic line bundles with the required boundary-completion identifications, continuous local CLD positivity gives positive local mixed measures.

links.label: Strong first-energy completion
Positivity of specified Yuan–Zhang local mixed measures

nodes.title: Larger domains and classical representatives
nodes.summary: Find domain and background conditions giving barriers, Green formulas, boundary tightness and stable exhaustion. Separately characterize completed classes that admit canonical ambient classical plurisubharmonic representatives, with precise boundary and pointwise detection statements.

links.label: Problem: Domain and boundary extension
Problem: Classical representatives of completed classes

nodes.title: Finite-energy Green products
nodes.summary: Construct Green classes with integrable truncation products and local cycle pairings. Prove approximation independence, symmetry and comparison with existing smooth, formal and delta theories under explicit intersection hypotheses.

links.label: Problem: Finite-energy Green products

nodes.title: Adelic finite-energy intersection
nodes.summary: Combine local finite-energy metric-change formulas with explicit placewise summability and boundary control. The proposed global pairing requires its own approximation, projection and positivity theorems.

links.label: Problem: Adelic finite-energy intersection
